newsitem.title: FRANCE: Klima, Chirac back broad EMU, say treaty flexible.
newsitem.headline: Klima, Chirac back broad EMU, say treaty flexible.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima said on Friday he and French President Jacques Chirac agreed there should be no delay to European monetary union, they wanted as many countries as possible in from the start and the treaty was flexible enough to allow more than a mathematical decision.

"There was agreement that the economically and politically important project of EMU should not be postponed," Klima told a news conference after meetings with Chirac and French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis. "To do so would cause great politcal and economic damage."
"It (EMU) should be launched on January 1, 1999 with the biggest possible number of member states," Klima said.

"We also agreed that we need not, and must not, change the stability criteria but that the existing treaty gives enough flexibility for the heads of state and government to take a wise political decision, and not just for a mathematical exercise," he said. Klima's visit, his first to Paris since taking office, was set against the background of a French parliamentary election which takes place in two rounds on May 25 and June 1.

He told reporters after meeting Arthuis that he would offer no opinion about which party in the election he supported but that he could not meet opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin because the latter could not be in Paris on Friday.

The Socialist party has called during the campaign for a more politicial dimension to European monetary union and for more emphasis on growth and employment in the drive to a single currency in the European Union.

Among the ideas it is pushing is an economic government with greater teeth than the planned 'stability council', which would amount to an informal gathering of finance ministers for the countries participating in the euro single currency.
Earlier, after talks with Finance Minister Jean Arthuis, Klima said a political counterweight to the future European central bank was important.

"It is very important that in addition to an independent European central bank there be a council of stability, a forum that can assure the coordination of economic, financial and monetary policy that we need in Europe," he told reporters.
